inspection.policy: Only exact pass or fail; partial and ambiguous evidence is fail.

target_gates.evidence: A dominant glass-front astronomical clock fills the right side, with several concentric numbered rings and a clearly visible lunar/eclipse disk.

Many gears and a large coiled spring are visible, but no independently recognizable anchor escapement or balance assembly is legible as the third connected component; partial mechanism evidence fails the all-component gate.
The woman’s hand visibly wraps a large brass key and its long shaft is clearly inserted into the clock case.
A mechanical bird is visible in front of the lower mechanism, but an open hinged escapement cage and a halfway-inside/halfway-out emergence state are not visible, so causal release is ambiguous.
The room contains a wall-scale network of gears, multiple suspended pocket watches, and calibration or repair tools on the worktable.

nearest_neighbor_rejection_gates.evidence: Clock faces, gears, spring mechanism, and winding key dominate; boiler, steam plume, and pipework do not dominate the visible scene.
The inserted oversized key and exposed working mechanism create an active clockwork event rather than a passive luxury-watch portrait.

common_photo_reference_gates.evidence: Exactly one clearly adult woman is the principal human subject, with an unobscured adult face and proportions.

Broad appearance cues are visibly consistent with the appearance-only reference: long near-black wavy hair, warm brown eyes, softly arched brows, oval face, and natural rose lips. Biometric identity is not evaluated.
Face, gripping hand, inserted key, glass case, and foreground mechanism are photographically coherent, with no obvious duplicate limb, malformed key contact, or contradictory foreground perspective.
